newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's newly-elected parliament to meet on May 18.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's newly-elected parliament to meet on May 18.

text.p: President Ali Abdullah Saleh ordered Yemen's newly-elected parliament on Tuesday to hold its first session on May 18, the official SABA news agency said.
The 301-seat chamber was elected on April 27 in the first general elections since a 1994 civil war which nearly tore the country apart.

President Saleh's ruling General People's Congress (GPC) won a 187-seat majority in parliament while the Islah Party, its junior Islamist coalition partner in the outgoing chamber, won 53 seats, Yemen's Supreme Elections Committee said on Monday.
Independents won 54 seats and two opposition parties took a total of five seats, it said in a statement read on television.
Results in two constituencies have yet to be announced but the committee described the latest figures as final results of the polls.

The main opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP), some of whose leaders launched a secessionist bid that launched the civil war, and three others boycotted the elections to protest alleged irregularities. The government denied the charges.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123, Islah 62, and the main opposition Yemen Socialist Party (YSP) 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties.
